real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates climbed to 7.43% as the 10-Year closed at 5.15%, the same rising rates that pushed Washington's interest bill past $1 trillion.
real_estate.commentary:
The bond market set the tone for housing today. The 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.15%, up 0.06, and MND's 30-year mortgage rose to 7.43% with the 15-year at 7.07%. Those same higher rates are why the federal interest bill topped $1 trillion this fiscal year, as the Economy section shows.

On our five city median list price of $1,084,000 with 20% down, principal and interest now run about $6,022 a month, about $35 more than at Friday's 7.37%. Small moves add up on Bay Area loan sizes.

Locally, the five city ledger rose to 681 from 679, with Hayward at 191 from 188 and Milpitas at 104 from 102, while Fremont slipped to 227 from 231. The board wide table eased to 2,651 from 2,662, and brand new listings fell to 198 from 209.

What this means for you: on days when rates jump, buyers with a rate lock plan ready before they write an offer are the ones who stay calm. With 175 homes on the ledger sitting 60 days or longer, there is still room to negotiate, and sellers who price to the comps are the ones getting offers.

• Board wide: 2,651 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 139 coming soon and 198 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 681 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 608 are on the market and 73 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 227 live, 181 active, 27 coming soon, 16 brand new and 3 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,298,500 at $800 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 39 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 191, Milpitas 104, Newark 94, Union City 65.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,084,000 at $678 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 175 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.news:
Chip stocks led a rebound after last week's sell-off. Intel rose 2.43%, AMD 1.76% and Nvidia 1.38%, lifting the Nasdaq 1.11% while the Dow finished nearly flat. Netflix reports Tuesday, kicking off a busy earnings week.

Today is the 39th anniversary of Black Monday, when the Dow fell 22.61% in one session, from 2,246.74 to 1,738.74. It is still the worst day on record; at today's close, a day like that would erase about 11,750 points. Two of the five worst days came in March 2020, and the Dow closed back above its February 2020 record by November 16 that year. This Monday, thankfully, behaved.

economy.note: Gold and silver are Monday, October 19 settlements (COMEX December); the 10-Year is Monday's Treasury close; Brent is Friday's ICE December settlement, the latest one our source has settled.
economy.commentary:
The federal interest bill topped $1 trillion. Net interest on the debt reached $1.05 trillion in fiscal 2026, which ended September 30, according to the Treasury's September statement, up from $970 billion a year earlier and $241 billion in fiscal 2016. That is 19.5% of federal receipts, close to Market Briefs' one dollar of every five.

Rates are doing as much of the work as the size of the debt. The average rate Treasury pays on its marketable debt is 3.52%, up from 1.47% in September 2021, and the 10-Year closed Monday at 5.15%. It turns out Uncle Sam has a rate problem too.

A correction on Friday's numbers: the newsletter printed Brent at $107.99, down 1.69%, but Friday's settlement was $109.86, up 3.72%, and it had the 10-Year at 5.06% where Treasury's close was 5.09%.
